## Root group

Key: implement-default-vpn-dns
Kind: group
Project: orbit
Parent: none
Depends on: none
Title: Implement ORB-242 — default VPN DNS on managed peers
Objective: Managed peers resolve private and ordinary names through Orbit VPN DNS, and an operator can repair existing peers without reprovisioning their roles or restarting their tunnel.
Child order: default-resolver, repair-existing-peer
Sibling dependencies: default-resolver has none; repair-existing-peer depends only on default-resolver.

Scope in: the published issue's managed DNS selection, retained resolver state and recovery, Gateway-local DNS-only maintenance, and operator documentation.
Scope out: LAN-specific central answers; private DNS record ownership; Route names and placement; Cluster lifecycle expansion; macOS overrides; local DNS services on peers; WireGuard topology changes; new API/SDK/client-CLI surfaces; harness changes; production rollout.

Each assignment includes this root brief, the exact approved and published issue contract, and its own task brief. An implementer does not need this conversation.

## Shared context and code evidence

Resolve all source paths below against the Orbit repository at the recorded baseline.

- docs/decisions/0061-use-vpn-dns-by-default-on-managed-peers.md is accepted on main and owns default managed-peer resolution, override preservation, and recovery. ADR 0062 is accepted but its LAN-DNS implementation is excluded here.
- docs/decisions/0023-separate-hostname-selection-from-cluster-routing.md preserves Route hostname and scope ownership. docs/decisions/0033-trust-wireguard-members-for-private-node-traffic.md preserves network trust.
- apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/WireGuard/NativeWireGuardPeerConverger.php publishes Node.tld with the VPN suffix, selects wireguard/underlay/operator DNS modes, and owns immediate and retained recovery. Its persisted domain validation accepts the root domain token, but end-to-end root-domain behavior is not yet tested.
- apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/WireGuard/VpnConfigurationRepository.php resolves DNS overrides and whether DNS is reached over WireGuard. Keep explicit overrides distinguishable from the managed default; do not infer that every address inside the VPN subnet is an unmodified default.
- apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/AppDev/RemoteAppDevTldRouteManager.php and NativeAppDevTldConverger.php are additional writers of resolver selection. A default-resolver repair must not be undone by a supported TLD operation.
- apps/gateway/app/Infrastructure/WireGuard/UplinkDnsResolvers.php and docs/solutions/vpn-dnsmasq-uplink-resolvers.md describe upstream selection and the self-recursion hazard. The VPN DNS host is not a managed peer target for the DNS-only maintenance command.
- apps/gateway/app/Console/Commands/ProvisionNodeCommand.php and RetargetNodeCommand.php provide existing Gateway-local administrative entry-point conventions. No DNS-only command exists at this baseline.
- The existing tests/Feature/Infrastructure/WireGuard/NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php includes executable shell coverage, distinct and null TLD cases, and multi-domain immediate/retained rollback. Reuse those harnesses inside Gateway tests; do not change the external Incus harness.
- docs/reference/private-dns.md does not exist yet and is assigned below. docs/reference/routes.md describes route selection, not a peer resolver setup recipe.

## Published issue contract at preparation approval

Managed Linux peers resolve private Route names and ordinary internet names through Orbit VPN DNS by default, under [ADR 0061](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0061-use-vpn-dns-by-default-on-managed-peers.md>). An operator can bring an existing managed peer onto the same resolver policy without reprovisioning its roles or restarting its WireGuard tunnel. Explicit DNS overrides and client-owned configuration remain intact.

The original incident was observed on 12 September 2026 against Gateway version `7b0e9402`, matching inspected main `7b0e9402681e48db21da847812439d0da1f25344`. The issue was re-evaluated after the accepted DNS decisions at `7955dc5c10121f49ffb212c9fc7bf8d01e50ec06`.

Observed topology: active Cluster `dev` (4), TLD `test`; Router Beast (9), `10.44.0.7`; workload Node Sabre (12), `10.44.0.10`, `tld=null`; Orbit DNS `10.44.0.1`; AppInstance 6 and Route 5, `tasks.commander.test`.

Reproduction from the affected Node before local repair:

```sh
resolvectl status orbit
getent ahostsv4 tasks.commander.test
dig +noall +answer @10.44.0.1 tasks.commander.test A
curl --resolve tasks.commander.test:443:10.44.0.7 \
  --cacert /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/orbit-managed-root-ca.crt \
  https://tasks.commander.test/projects/orbit/tasks
```

The link used DNS server `10.44.0.1` but only domain `~orbit`. Normal lookup failed, while the explicit DNS query returned `10.44.0.7` and forced-resolution HTTPS returned 200 with valid TLS. `/etc/wireguard/orbit.conf` and `orbit.dns-link` also contained only the VPN suffix. The peer converger supplies `$node->tld`; Route hostname selection separately supports the active Cluster TLD fallback.

A local operational repair added `~test` to the saved DNS hooks, DNS state record, and live resolver on Sabre without restarting WireGuard. Normal lookup and HTTPS then passed through Beast, and ordinary internet DNS still worked. This is not a product fix: managed reprovisioning can write the incomplete domain list again. Shark has the same nullable Node TLD in inventory, but its resolver was not verified because SSH host-key verification failed.

## Scope

* In: managed peer DNS selection during provisioning, persistent DNS hooks, retained DNS state, retry, and recovery.
* In: a Gateway-local maintenance command that repairs DNS for one existing managed peer without role reprovisioning.
* In: operator documentation for default resolution, explicit overrides, inspection, DNS-only repair, and failure recovery.
* Out: requester-specific LAN DNS answers, private DNS record ownership, Router selection, Node and Cluster naming changes, and unsupported Cluster lifecycle transitions.
* Out: local DNS servers on managed peers, hosts-file workarounds, macOS resolver changes, WireGuard peer topology changes, application transport changes, and frontend development-server routing.
* Out: new public Gateway API, SDK, or Orbit client CLI operations; the maintenance entry point runs on the Gateway.
* Out: harness code changes and live-fleet rollout.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A newly provisioned managed peer without an explicit DNS override uses Orbit VPN DNS for both private and ordinary names, including an app-dev Node with a null Node TLD in an active Cluster. Proof: extend `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Infrastructure/WireGuard/NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php`; on disposable Incus Nodes inspect `resolvectl status` and observe private and ordinary queries reaching the VPN DNS listener.
- [ ] A generated Cluster Route and an exact Route outside the peer's Node or Cluster suffix resolve through the normal OS resolver without adding a local suffix, DNS server service, or hostname record. Proof: publish both names in an Incus discovery topology, compare `getent ahostsv4` with an explicit `dig` query to Orbit DNS, and inspect the peer before and after publication.
- [ ] A deterministic workload responds over its ordinary HTTPS Route through a separate Router with certificate verification enabled and without a hosts override or `--resolve`. Proof: ordinary `curl` in the same Incus topology.
- [ ] Repeated provisioning and a controlled restart of a disposable peer retain the same intended resolver selection in live state, persistent hooks, and retained recovery state while general IP routes remain unchanged. Proof: extend `NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php` and compare `resolvectl status` and `ip route` before and after those operations in Incus.
- [ ] The Gateway-local DNS-only maintenance command refuses a missing, inactive, operator-owned, or VPN-server target before remote mutation; for one eligible peer it repairs live and persisted DNS, is repeatable, and preserves the running WireGuard tunnel, private keys, role services, and workload placement. Proof: add command acceptance tests in `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Console` and run the new command twice against a disposable peer with legacy split-DNS state.
- [ ] Failure at a DNS publication boundary restores the preceding resolver configuration or retains explicit recoverable failure state without reporting success; immediate and retained recovery preserve all prior managed domains, explicit overrides, and unrelated interface configuration. Proof: extend the immediate and retained rollback cases in `NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php`, add DNS-only repair failure tests, and inject a resolver failure on a disposable peer.
- [ ] An explicit DNS override and client-owned operator configuration retain their established behavior, and ordinary queries forwarded by Orbit VPN DNS do not recurse into its own listener. Proof: extend `NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php` and `apps/gateway/tests/Unit/Infrastructure/WireGuard/UplinkDnsResolversTest.php`; observe upstream forwarding and an override-equipped peer in Incus.
- [ ] Operators can inspect resolver selection, run the documented Gateway-local repair, identify its failure state, and distinguish DNS configuration from application IP routing without editing private keys. Proof: follow `docs/reference/private-dns.md` on a disposable affected peer and run `composer docs-lint`.

issue.title: Use Orbit VPN DNS by default on managed peers
issue.description:
Managed Linux peers resolve private Route names and ordinary internet names through Orbit VPN DNS by default, under [ADR 0061](<https://github.com/nckrtl/orbit/blob/main/docs/decisions/0061-use-vpn-dns-by-default-on-managed-peers.md>). An operator can bring an existing managed peer onto the same resolver policy without reprovisioning its roles or restarting its WireGuard tunnel. Explicit DNS overrides and client-owned configuration remain intact.

The original incident was observed on 12 September 2026 against Gateway version `7b0e9402`, matching inspected main `7b0e9402681e48db21da847812439d0da1f25344`. The issue was re-evaluated after the accepted DNS decisions at `7955dc5c10121f49ffb212c9fc7bf8d01e50ec06`.

Observed topology: active Cluster `dev` (4), TLD `test`; Router Beast (9), `10.44.0.7`; workload Node Sabre (12), `10.44.0.10`, `tld=null`; Orbit DNS `10.44.0.1`; AppInstance 6 and Route 5, `tasks.commander.test`.

Reproduction from the affected Node before local repair:

```sh
resolvectl status orbit
getent ahostsv4 tasks.commander.test
dig +noall +answer @10.44.0.1 tasks.commander.test A
curl --resolve tasks.commander.test:443:10.44.0.7 \
  --cacert /usr/local/share/ca-certificates/orbit-managed-root-ca.crt \
  https://tasks.commander.test/projects/orbit/tasks
```

The link used DNS server `10.44.0.1` but only domain `~orbit`. Normal lookup failed, while the explicit DNS query returned `10.44.0.7` and forced-resolution HTTPS returned 200 with valid TLS. `/etc/wireguard/orbit.conf` and `orbit.dns-link` also contained only the VPN suffix. The peer converger supplies `$node->tld`; Route hostname selection separately supports the active Cluster TLD fallback.

A local operational repair added `~test` to the saved DNS hooks, DNS state record, and live resolver on Sabre without restarting WireGuard. Normal lookup and HTTPS then passed through Beast, and ordinary internet DNS still worked. This is not a product fix: managed reprovisioning can write the incomplete domain list again. Shark has the same nullable Node TLD in inventory, but its resolver was not verified because SSH host-key verification failed.

## Scope

* In: managed peer DNS selection during provisioning, persistent DNS hooks, retained DNS state, retry, and recovery.
* In: a Gateway-local maintenance command that repairs DNS for one existing managed peer without role reprovisioning.
* In: operator documentation for default resolution, explicit overrides, inspection, DNS-only repair, and failure recovery.
* Out: requester-specific LAN DNS answers, private DNS record ownership, Router selection, Node and Cluster naming changes, and unsupported Cluster lifecycle transitions.
* Out: local DNS servers on managed peers, hosts-file workarounds, macOS resolver changes, WireGuard peer topology changes, application transport changes, and frontend development-server routing.
* Out: new public Gateway API, SDK, or Orbit client CLI operations; the maintenance entry point runs on the Gateway.
* Out: harness code changes and live-fleet rollout.

## Acceptance

- [ ] A newly provisioned managed peer without an explicit DNS override uses Orbit VPN DNS for both private and ordinary names, including an app-dev Node with a null Node TLD in an active Cluster. Proof: extend `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Infrastructure/WireGuard/NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php`; on disposable Incus Nodes inspect `resolvectl status` and observe private and ordinary queries reaching the VPN DNS listener.
- [ ] A generated Cluster Route and an exact Route outside the peer's Node or Cluster suffix resolve through the normal OS resolver without adding a local suffix, DNS server service, or hostname record. Proof: publish both names in an Incus discovery topology, compare `getent ahostsv4` with an explicit `dig` query to Orbit DNS, and inspect the peer before and after publication.
- [ ] A deterministic workload responds over its ordinary HTTPS Route through a separate Router with certificate verification enabled and without a hosts override or `--resolve`. Proof: ordinary `curl` in the same Incus topology.
- [ ] Repeated provisioning and a controlled restart of a disposable peer retain the same intended resolver selection in live state, persistent hooks, and retained recovery state while general IP routes remain unchanged. Proof: extend `NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php` and compare `resolvectl status` and `ip route` before and after those operations in Incus.
- [ ] The Gateway-local DNS-only maintenance command refuses a missing, inactive, operator-owned, or VPN-server target before remote mutation; for one eligible peer it repairs live and persisted DNS, is repeatable, and preserves the running WireGuard tunnel, private keys, role services, and workload placement. Proof: add command acceptance tests in `apps/gateway/tests/Feature/Console` and run the new command twice against a disposable peer with legacy split-DNS state.
- [ ] Failure at a DNS publication boundary restores the preceding resolver configuration or retains explicit recoverable failure state without reporting success; immediate and retained recovery preserve all prior managed domains, explicit overrides, and unrelated interface configuration. Proof: extend the immediate and retained rollback cases in `NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php`, add DNS-only repair failure tests, and inject a resolver failure on a disposable peer.
- [ ] An explicit DNS override and client-owned operator configuration retain their established behavior, and ordinary queries forwarded by Orbit VPN DNS do not recurse into its own listener. Proof: extend `NativeWireGuardPeerConvergerTest.php` and `apps/gateway/tests/Unit/Infrastructure/WireGuard/UplinkDnsResolversTest.php`; observe upstream forwarding and an override-equipped peer in Incus.
- [ ] Operators can inspect resolver selection, run the documented Gateway-local repair, identify its failure state, and distinguish DNS configuration from application IP routing without editing private keys. Proof: follow `docs/reference/private-dns.md` on a disposable affected peer and run `composer docs-lint`.
